observation: PMP, Ham, French Road Rules, and Solar recorded zero processed units in retained early windows; PMP/Ham were absent from sampled first result sets, French had narrow bilingual discoverability, and Solar lacked a meaningful direct homeowner-book shelf.
interpretation: A real problem or useful book does not establish Amazon-native discovery or conversion.
lesson: Keep opportunity evidence, book intent, Amazon intent, discoverability, click appeal, conversion, and economics separate.
validation_required: Repeat fixed-query D14/D30 snapshots for a new cohort.
next_test: D0/D14 discovery capture with retained query set.

observation: Early zero-unit outcomes lack complete impressions, verified visibility, and conversion data.
interpretation: Zero sales alone cannot distinguish weak demand, discoverability, click appeal, conversion, or economics.
lesson: Do not diagnose demand or conversion from zero sales without marketplace-state evidence.
scope: All book launches with incomplete visibility data
validation_required: Operational use on a future launch.
next_test: Record D0 and D14 snapshots before interpretation.

observation: Odyssey's source-plus-language query produced a short, legible result set and one early print order; the catalogue has additional observed unit activity.
interpretation: A named source plus named language can form a repeatable micro-market product system.
lesson: Treat Toki Pona as a positive control and system-cell hypothesis, not evidence for portfolio-scale revenue.
validation_required: Separate repeat/series effects from source-query discovery.
next_test: Compare a system cell with a standalone cell.

observation: A cheap linked-story prototype required a commercial audit, source mechanism screen, architecture gate, and approximately 10k-word prose test before a full-draft recommendation could be earned.
interpretation: Prototype quality is evidence to test, not sunk-cost justification for a novel.
lesson: For generated fiction, place commercial and architecture gates before bulk drafting; use bounded prose to test whether causality and protagonist pressure survive actual scenes.
validation_required: Apply to a second fiction project.
next_test: Draft approved Bracken Ford anchors without expanding the full manuscript.

observation: The source pool became usable only after its material was reduced to abstract dramatic mechanisms; standalone anecdote structure did not supply novel causality.
interpretation: Interesting source anecdotes are not chapter candidates by default.
lesson: Record mechanism, transformation, and causal function; reject anything that cannot survive deep transformation.
validation_required: Use in the next source-led fiction experiment.
next_test: Check provenance before any future publication-oriented draft.

observation: Existing runs retain source packs, production contracts, deterministic QA, visual contact sheets, release preflight, format-specific state, and Jekyll source/entity pre-production artifacts.
interpretation: Source provenance, format-specific QA, and preflight are reusable production controls; Jekyll does not yet validate the whole pipeline.
lesson: Treat a book's source, semantic/entity handling, layout QA, and each publication format as separate gates.
scope: Toki Pona and structured book production
validation_required: Complete an approved new title through all gates.
next_test: Run only the authorised Jekyll pre-production gate.

observation: Observed catalogue activity supports a small repeatable Toki Pona thesis, while Radar evidence does not establish the broader portfolio revenue target.
interpretation: Repeatability in a niche is not scaling evidence.
lesson: Keep catalogue thesis, book-level actuals, and portfolio-goal claims separate.
validation_required: Retain enough visibility and cost data over multiple releases.
next_test: Capture actuals and repeat-buyer signals without changing selection logic.

observation: No book-insert narrative-comics experiment has yet been run; Pictiq's protected vocabulary and renderer are independently owned.
interpretation: Narrative illustration needs a comprehension benchmark before it can be treated as a product feature.
lesson: Do not add symbols/operators for a book; record vocabulary pressure separately and test blind comprehension against author intent.
validation_required: Execute approved Jekyll and Bracken Ford samples.
next_test: Request approval for the first two sample comics.

observation: Toki Pona production supplies visual-language and layout evidence; Bracken Ford supplies narrative relations; Radar supplies later discovery measurement.
interpretation: The systems can exchange test cases and measurement methods without merging ownership or implying sales effects.
lesson: Use cross-project links as bounded experiment inputs, never as automatic integration or commercial proof.
validation_required: Run one approved narrative-comics benchmark.
next_test: Compare two book contexts under one frozen Pictiq protocol.

run_product: Jekyll pre-production and RN3 bilingual reference
observation: Jekyll has a normalized public-domain source, source manifest, representative sample, and explicit entity ledger; RN3 retains a source ledger and bilingual factual QA.
interpretation: Source normalization and entity decisions can be made deterministic enough to audit, but semantic and proper-name choices still require human review.
lesson: Keep source ingestion, translation/entity decisions, and factual language QA as separate artifacts; do not call a sample a complete translation pipeline.
scope: Toki Pona translation and entity handling
validation_required: Repeat on the next complete title.
next_test: Run the Jekyll entity ledger through full pre-production before translation expansion.

observation: RN2 and RN3 retain deterministic checks, full-book contact sheets, high-risk page sheets, and release preflight separated by format.
interpretation: Technical validity and visual/editorial validity are different gates that can be reused across titles.
lesson: Keep EPUB/PDF/KDP format checks separate from human visual and semantic review; automate regressions, not taste.
scope: Toki Pona book layout and publication QA
validation_required: Apply the gate to the next new title.
next_test: Record manual interventions and automated pass/fail separately for Jekyll.

observation: Source normalization and sample layout are automated, while the sample QA explicitly retains model/editorial review and does not authorize full-book production.
interpretation: Automation reduces repeatable preparation work but does not establish semantic or product readiness.
lesson: Promote deterministic preparation scripts only with a human editorial gate at the next boundary.
validation_required: Measure manual intervention on a complete title.
next_test: Log every manual correction during the approved Jekyll pre-production gate.

observation: The reusable narrative runner and provider adapter are structurally ready, but the first real-provider request could not run because the trusted local model worker was unavailable.
interpretation: Provider availability is a separate gate from orchestration correctness; fixture output must not be relabelled as real translation evidence.
lesson: Fail closed at the provider boundary and rerun the exact sample only after a real trusted provider is available.
validation_required: Repeat with a working provider and measure review burden.
next_test: Start or approve the local model worker, then run V3 semantic QA and second-pass measurement.

run_product: Historical Toki Pona path forensic audit
observation: Retained Odyssey workflow evidence shows interactive ChatGPT continuation/glossary batches followed by manual ODT assembly and editorial correction; neither the public translator nor abvx-local-model-worker is evidenced as the historical prose generator.
interpretation: For an established production system, current provider configuration must not replace reconstruction of the last known successful path.
lesson: Reconstruct retained production evidence before introducing or selecting a new provider; preserve the narrative control layer and replace only the provider seam.
scope: Toki Pona provider selection and narrative pipeline
validation_required: Repeat on the next provider-backed narrative run.
next_test: Connect an authenticated capable model path and rerun the unchanged Jekyll sample.

observation: OPENAI_API_KEY was present and the existing Responses API boundary was reused, but DNS/egress failure prevented the first real request; no fallback or synthetic translation was accepted.
interpretation: Credential presence is not equivalent to provider reachability; authenticated quality gates need a distinct network/provider availability check.
lesson: Fail closed on pre-response network errors and preserve the exact smoke selection for rerun from a network-capable environment.
validation_required: Run the same five-block smoke with real output before any 40-block regression.
next_test: Rerun V5 where api.openai.com resolves and is reachable.

observation: Local OpenAI connectivity and gpt-5.6-sol output are confirmed. The original medium/2400 run completed three blocks but starved two; low/3000 retries completed both failed blocks. Raw Responses output must be parsed from output[].content[].text and completion status must be checked independently of visible text.
interpretation: Reasoning budget and visible-output budget interact materially for literary translation; non-empty partial text is not a successful provider result.
lesson: Use low reasoning with a bounded visible-output budget as the next candidate configuration, preserve mixed-run metadata, and require independent semantic QA before scaling from five to forty blocks.
validation_required: Run exact 40-block regression with checkpoint/resume and bounded max-token retry.
next_test: Execute the real 40-block Jekyll regression; do not translate the full book.

run_product: Jekyll V7 targeted second-pass semantic re-QA
observation: The real low-reasoning 40-block regression completed 40/40 with zero retries. Five targeted second passes repaired all five material defect cases: two FIXED and three IMPROVED_BUT_REVIEW, with no NOT_FIXED or REGRESSED cases.
interpretation: For this Jekyll pipeline, low reasoning is both operationally robust and adequate when paired with risk-based targeted repair and chapter-level editorial review.
lesson: Promote gpt-5.6-sol low/3000 as the current Jekyll primary configuration, but keep targeted second pass and human literary review as mandatory gates; do not generalize beyond this title.
validation_required: Measure full-book review burden during the authorized production run.
next_test: Start the bounded full-book Jekyll production run under V2 plan.

run_product: No Further Claims structural expansion V2
observation: V1 had 11 chapters and 11,249 whole-file words with a compressed middle and duplicate test variants. V2 has 13 chapters and 25,094 whole-file words (25,071 body words); consequential choices in Chapters 4–9 feed one hearing, one bag incident, and a partial path outcome. Structural gate: HUMAN_EDIT_GO, middle WORKABLE.
interpretation: In one project, expanding through causal choices and costs produced a complete short-novel draft without reverting to detachable anecdote logic; reader and sales quality remain untested.
lesson: For an anchors-first draft with a weak middle, add scenes that alter evidence, relationships, cost, decisions, and viability; remove duplicate event versions and development scaffolding before the human-edit gate.
system_change_candidate: Causal-scene expansion and duplicate-event cleanup gate
validation_required: Independent human developmental read of V2 and targeted revision.
next_test: Human editorial assessment of V2; no automatic further expansion.

run_product: No Further Claims / Bracken Ford post-production
observation: The run reached author-reported Kindle submission/publishing and paperback submission/in-review. Local project retained multiple review/development files, and its illustration manifest still named an obsolete review manuscript/placement. The lock hash stayed stable through final interior attribution. The first final-interior candidate had a Pictiq copyright block crossing the KDP safe-area boundary; its successor passed. Local packaging lacked origin records for the six composite illustrations/cover. Print art was about 195 effective DPI and passed human visual proof; Kindle Previewer was unavailable locally while local EPUB checks passed. A generated wrap candidate showed a barcode-zone placeholder though KDP supplies the barcode.
interpretation: The production run exposed control-plane gaps around canonical pointers, per-asset provenance, safe-area checks, cover inputs, and environment-specific Kindle validation. Existing full-page visual QA and external preview gates remain complementary; the evidence does not establish a redundant gate or general print-resolution threshold.
lesson: Maintain a canonical manifest; separate STRUCTURE_COMPLETE from PRODUCT_COMPLETE; scan reader-facing cleanliness before editorial acceptance; allow early illustration exploration but finalize placement after structural/editorial lock; preserve the Pictiq source-to-composite chain; require per-asset provenance before Amazon packaging; treat <300 DPI as a print-risk gate; keep EPUB_VALID distinct from KINDLE_RENDER_VERIFIED; reserve the barcode zone for background unless using a real publisher barcode; after TEXT_LOCKED permit prose edits only for TYPO, DEMONSTRATED_FACTUAL_ERROR, or PRODUCTION_FORMATTING_DEFECT; freeze metadata and capture D0/D7/D14/D30 after product/text lock.
scope: Book Factory; one fiction title for print/EPUB/KDP
system_change_candidate: Canonical manifest, asset provenance schema, and explicit publication QA checklist
validation_required: Apply to the next book and compare manual corrections, missing provenance, and preview defects; verify Bracken Ford live URLs/identifiers when available.
next_test: Return production focus to the Jekyll Toki Pona provider regression.

run_product: No Further Claims: A Bracken Ford Novel / publication D0
observation: Authenticated KDP Bookshelf showed Kindle and paperback Live on 2026-09-23 at $2.99 and $9.99, with KDP Select enrollment. Amazon detail pages showed Kindle ASIN B0HKTBFFJM, paperback ASIN B0HKTFR8ND, ISBN 9798176597592, and publication date 2026-09-23. France-session retail purchase/shipping was blocked at the selected location, and cross-format links were not visible. Title-filtered processed-orders report for Sep 1-23 showed 0 Kindle, 0 print, 0 total; title-specific KENP, royalties, reviews, and placed orders remain unknown. Nine signed-in personalized non-title search checks excluded three 'Previously viewed' modules from organic evidence. Production facts: 20,381 body words, 13 chapters, 62-page 6x9 B&W paperback, six full-page assets, four Pictiq comics, Kindle and paperback.
interpretation: The novel is verified live on KDP in both formats, but location-specific retail access and format-family linking remain unresolved. A zero processed-order count at D0 is not a commercial outcome, and a personalized search shelf is not a clean indexing test.
lesson: Capture publication state from Bookshelf and retail pages; record actual metadata separately from intended package values; filter KDP reports by title; preserve UNKNOWN where a title-level metric was not observed; exclude personalized recommendation modules from organic discovery; keep a dated D0 baseline and unchanged D7/D14/D30 schedule before making a product or pricing conclusion.
scope: One fiction title, one new pen name, one publication-day observation
validation_required: Recheck supported-territory availability and cross-format retail links; repeat the nine discovery queries under comparable conditions; inspect title-filtered KENP and royalty reports at D7/D14/D30.
next_test: Return factory focus to the Jekyll Toki Pona provider regression.

run_product: Jekyll Toki Pona full primary translation V1
observation: The 462-block full run retained 351 successful source-hash-matching gpt-5.6-sol checkpoints and 111 failures after a generic HTTP 429 at chapter 10 block 14. Owner reported API balance fell from above USD 7 to -USD 0.29; this supports credit/quota exhaustion but the retained failure lacks provider error code/body. Successful usage summed to 986,926 input tokens (985,873 cache writes, zero cached reads), 154,949 output tokens (102,724 reasoning included), and 126,579 translation characters. Current official GPT-5.6 Sol pricing reprices the successful usage at about USD 8.03. The old runner continued after a persistent error; no call/token cost gate stopped the job.
interpretation: Technical reliability and semantic consistency did not guarantee economical execution. A linear primary-cost projection is USD 10.66 for the 25,622-word source, but the estimate is not an invoice and quality/value are not priced. Repeated full-ledger prompts and zero observed cache reads increased input cost; alternate prompts/models/batches have untested quality risk.
lesson: Require a preflight recording source scope, request/token estimates, current official model/cache pricing, primary plus QA cost, verified balance or UNKNOWN, an owner-approved ceiling, and hard call/token caps. Stop immediately on persistent quota/auth/account/model/unknown-429 errors; bound retries for explicit transient failures. Record provider/model/prompt version/hash/config per new block. Never silently change the model or prompt for a partial book; preserve all successful checkpoints.
scope: One 25,622-word public-domain translation run and its local provider runner
system_change_candidate: Cost preflight, max-calls plus cumulative-token runner caps, and per-block prompt/model provenance
validation_required: For any separately authorized completion, verify cost preflight and caps; run bounded prompt-cache/entity-subset/model/batch regressions before changing production strategy.
next_test: No production run now. Await explicit cost ceiling/balance authorization before deciding between unchanged Sol and a regression-gated optimization.
